solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurry on by to see holiday apartment

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows the first, as it is set on it

parts.note: by as in multiplication, two by three meaning two times three
to hare is to run fast, to hurry

explanation.surface: Someone rushing past to view a holiday flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link word here: it is the multiplication sign, as in three by four. 'on' sets the hurrying piece after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared-ownership arrangement where each owner uses the property for set weeks, typically a holiday flat.

clue.text: Called out thanks to cast

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: through, as in 'success through hard work', means thanks to

explanation.surface: Someone shouts their gratitude to the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors, but it is the past tense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to cast a stone is to throw it.

clue.text: Bright spot in practice tests international body

parts.note: mocks are British school practice exams taken before the real ones
the UN, the United Nations

explanation.surface: A cheerful moment amid rehearsal exams for a world organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: MOCKS are trial exams sat in British schools before the real ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A parhelion, a luminous patch seen beside the sun in the sky caused by ice crystals.

clue.text: Sort of bike offering exercise, with appeal

parts.note: a sit-up is an abdominal exercise
and, joining things together, means with
to beg is to appeal or plead

explanation.surface: A bicycle marketed with a workout and some charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an old-fashioned upright bicycle whose rider sits erect, like a dog doing its trick.

clue.text: A hand put round brother, cowering?

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed around the next, enclosing it

parts.note: to give a hand is to aid
Fr is the abbreviation for Brother, as in a friar's title

explanation.surface: Someone puts a comforting arm round a frightened sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that cowering shows fear rather than meaning it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cowering is showing fright; the adjective names the fearful state behind it.

clue.text: In relief, the writer turned, told what to do?

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, giving me
bossed means ordered about, told what to do

explanation.surface: An author, relieved at last, after being ordered about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ME to EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoration standing out raised from a surface is said to be in relief.

clue.text: Shop less, arguably, after going around stores

indicators.note: going around means the held letters are read backwards
the phrase stores, holds within it, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A frugal shopper, arguably, does fewer rounds of the stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' takes SSARG from 'less, arguably'; 'going around' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, as a grass does.

clue.text: Sir's ultimately condescending — and sort of light

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: UV, ultraviolet, is a sort of light

explanation.surface: A knight's patronising remark about a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: GUV is British slang for governor, a respectful address to a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal address for a man in charge, used where one might say mister or boss.

clue.text: Men arriving in time to fool one: that's known in advance

indicators.note: the men arrive in the word, taking the place of its last letter

parts.note: April, whose first day is April Fools' Day
OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops turn up on April Fools' Day to trick someone, which was predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arriving in' puts OR in APRIL in place of its L, giving APRIOR; then add I.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase for reasoning from what is known beforehand, not from experience.

clue.text: Forged letters written out in bold

parts.note: sham means fake, forged
the letters L and S spelt as words, el and ess

explanation.surface: Fake letters typed up in heavy type.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter names EL and ESS spell out L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed, brazen: a person without any sense of disgrace acts boldly.

clue.text: Fat Hilary maybe briefly rocking scale

parts.note: rich food is fatty

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Hilary is a term at Oxford University and the law courts, January to March

explanation.surface: A plump person named Hilary rocks a set of scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilary' looks like a person but is a term of the academic year.
explanation.definitionFit: The earthquake magnitude scale named after seismologist Charles Richter measures the ground's shaking.

clue.text: Arab I transported across Bible Land

indicators.note: the rearranged letters spread across the next piece, enclosing it
transported, carried away, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AV, the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: An Arab carried through the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' turns ARABI into BARIA, which goes 'across' AV.
explanation.definitionFit: A Land is a German federal state; this southern one has Munich as its capital.

clue.text: Used to be clean after wiping hard

indicators.note: wiping out, removing, the letter from the word

parts.note: to wash is to clean
H, hard as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Something was once clean after a vigorous scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb meaning to exist, so it means existed or used to be.

clue.text: Where father hid pistols? Here, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A detective asks where the priest concealed the guns, suggesting this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tudor England, a hidden chamber sheltered Catholic priests from persecution.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret hiding places built in English houses for Catholic clergy, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Quiet pressman not having enough to explain

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ed, short for editor, a newspaperman
light on means short of, not having enough

explanation.surface: A silent journalist lacking sufficient material to clarify things.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning to clarify, to illuminate a matter so it is understood.

clue.text: Grilled bread and roast at first attempt

parts.note: to roast or pan is to criticise harshly
in one, as in getting it in one, with I for one

explanation.surface: Toasted sandwiches and a joint cooked successfully first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' means criticise, PAN; 'in one' is I as Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian toasted sandwiches, pressed in a ribbed grill.

clue.text: Upset, small twin rings and knocks

indicators.note: twin means the piece appears twice
upset in a down clue, so the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
S, the clothing size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A distressed little twin with rings knocks at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns HOOP over to POOH; 'twin' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully is to knock or disparage it.

clue.text: Number swarming around English holiday island

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the next letter

parts.note: ten is a number
rife means abounding, swarming

explanation.surface: Crowds of tourists swarm round an English visitor at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Canary Islands, a Spanish resort popular with British tourists.

clue.text: Did show behind curtains Italian backed and directed

indicators.note: curtains, as a verb, means encloses as a curtain does

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare bottom

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: It, short for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A performance behind the curtains, backed by an Italian director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did show behind' is the slang act of baring one's bottom; 'backed' gives TI, which 'curtains' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To gesture someone towards a place is to direct them there with a movement.

clue.text: Competition needs reserve, it's readily understood

parts.note: an open is a competition anyone may enter, as in golf
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A tournament needs a reserve player, as anyone can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a person or thing easily read and fully transparent.

clue.text: Title or medal for wrestling

indicators.note: the letters wrestle, struggle about, rearranging

explanation.surface: Wrestlers compete for a championship belt or a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or dignity of a nobleman, a hereditary title of the peerage.

clue.text: A record is entertaining, getting top marks

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record
has guests means is entertaining them

explanation.surface: An album that is fun to hear earns excellent grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Grade A marks; the Greek first letter stands for the highest score.

clue.text: Deprived person of sanctuary with books

parts.note: a haven is a sanctuary
OT, the Old Testament books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A needy person finding refuge with reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone poor or underprivileged, contrasted with the haves.

clue.text: Threads of story remain incomplete

parts.note: a fib is a story, a small lie

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to rest is to remain

explanation.surface: Plot strands of a tale left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine strands or filaments, the threads making up a fabric.

clue.text: Old man with kid: top in grand and thrilling sport

parts.note: pa, a father, an old man
to kid or rag is to tease
a lid is a top
G for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A father and child on a top in a grand, thrilling game.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaring from a height with a canopy wing, an exhilarating airborne pastime.

clue.text: Verse I felt that shows promise

parts.note: ow is what someone cries when they feel pain

explanation.surface: A poet says a line moved them, showing potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I felt that' is the cry of pain, OW.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn pledge or undertaking given to someone.

clue.text: One involved in joint exercise

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside

parts.note: a weld is a joint between metals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person takes part in a joint workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' is the verb, as in exercising power.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise power or authority is to wield it.

clue.text: Familiar address used by head

parts.note: used means old, secondhand
bean is slang for head

explanation.surface: A friendly form of address used by a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD BEAN is a dated British upper-class way to address a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A chummy, old-fashioned British term of address between friends.

clue.text: Girl's welcome from the floor

indicators.note: read from the floor upwards, so the down entry is backwards

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a welcome

explanation.surface: A young woman greeted by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the floor' sounds like audience input, but reverses AVE in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as in Eva Perón.

clue.text: Following on, batting to open the day

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: to cut open, sitting inside the other piece

parts.note: Tue, short for Tuesday
in, as a batsman at the crease is in

explanation.surface: A cricket report: following on, batting first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following on' is a cricket term, but 'on' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of attendants accompanying an important person, a following.

clue.text: A poem regularly reflecting on mostly sad state of islands

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter
reflecting means mirrored, read backwards
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A poem reflects at intervals on a gloomy island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' and 'reflecting' together give MOA, placed after the shortened 'sad' ('mostly').
explanation.definitionFit: An independent Pacific nation made up of islands.

clue.text: Not one boy attending Ladies College

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the boy comes along beside the rest

parts.note: Di, from Lady Di, the late Princess of Wales; Dis is its plural
uni, short for university
Ted, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad studying at a women's college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' is not a women's college: it is the plural of Di, as in Lady Di.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided, split apart, no longer acting together.
